claim: In the PFQG framework, when the triangulation is fine (large number of edges with small edge lengths), the dominant physics is described by a quantum field theory for general relativity coupled to matter on a smooth manifold, with a momentum cutoff proportional to the inverse average edge length.
falsifier: One can compute the effective action for a fine triangulation and verify that it matches a QFT with a cutoff given by the inverse average edge length.

conditions: the triangulation T(M) has a large number of edges
the cutoff is proportional to the inverse average edge length
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the formal derivation within the PFQG framework; the precise mapping to standard QFT may depend on the triangulation details.

title: Fine triangulation–dominant physics is QFT principle
